newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up, led by foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up, led by foreign buying.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed up on foreign buying of blue chips on Friday, with local investors focusing on low-valued scrips, brokers said.

The all share index closed 6.6 points up at 746.10. Price advances led losses by 57 to 24. Blue chips Aitken Spence rose 9.75 rupees to 165, Development Finance two to 280, and John Keells Holdings JKH.CM three 230.

"Foreign buying has been seen mainly among the highly capitalised blue chips and conglomerates, which are expected to benefit from good growth in plantations, tourism and manufacturing," said Shanil Perera of Lanka Securities.
Turnover was 152.2 million rupees, led by foreign buying of 470,000 Ceylon Tobacco shares, 556,999 Grains, 70,000 John Keells Holdings and 60,000 Development Finance.
The government said tourism arrivals so far in 1997 have risen by 17 percent due to better security, compared to a decline of 25 percent in 1996 due to separatist rebel attacks in the capital.
Plantation sector shares are seen doing well on the back of continuing demand for Sri Lanka tea from the Commonwealth of Independent States, analysts said.
They also said the crippling power crisis of 1996, which resulted from an over-dependence on hydro power, was not expected to be repeated in 1997 due to increased thermal power generation.
